Subject: Post-call: VentureTech competitive incident-response evaluation & next steps

Hi Alex — thanks again for your time earlier. Nice to meet you and the VentureTech team. Quick recap from our discovery + competitive evaluation conversation and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

Call highlights
- Primary ask: confirm how Redwood handles incident response, on-call escalation, RCA timelines, and SLA guarantees compared to hyperscalers and other inference APIs.
- Two deployment options in scope: Hosted API (fastest) and Dedicated (reserved capacity) for predictable performance and stronger isolation.
- You’ll run a short smoke test and a simulated outage test to validate failover and RCA process.

Immediate asks / proposed tests
1) We’ll provide an SLA & incident response comparison matrix (attached).
2) Proposed test: controlled failover/simulated outage on a non-prod project — 1 hour outage window, verification of KV cache and recovery time.
3) Log/retention expectations: we recommend 90 days for detailed audit logs for the test; we can adjust if your security team has different requirements.

What Redwood will provide
- Incident response matrix comparing Hosted vs Dedicated vs common hyperscaler endpoints (see attachment: incident_response_sla_matrix.pdf).
- Typical RCA cadence: initial acknowledgement within 1 hour for Sev1, preliminary findings within 72 hours, full RCA within 7 business days (scope permitting) — I’ll confirm exact wording with Marissa.
- On-call escalation path + PagerDuty contact for Dedicated customers.

Next steps
- Marissa to follow up with the formalized SLA/RCA wording and any redlines you should expect.
- Can we tentatively schedule the simulated outage test for next Thurs 2027-02-18 09:00–10:00 PT? If that works, we’ll send a test plan.
- Please send the security and procurement contacts (I see procurement@venturetech.com and security@venturetech.com in the thread; confirm preferred recipients).

Attachments: incident_response_sla_matrix.pdf, product_onepager.pdf

Thanks — I’ll keep this short and we can expand in the follow-up.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra

Thanks Rishi — useful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Our security team needs explicit SLA numbers (RPO/RTO if applicable) and the exact RCA commitment language for contract review. High level is helpful; we’ll need contract-ready wording.
- On the tests: the simulated outage is good. We prefer a brief pre-test run to exercise logging and alerting, then the outage simulation.
- Can you confirm who will be the PagerDuty escalation contact (name + role) during the test? We don’t want surprises.

I’ve cc’d procurement and security. Procurement will want pricing/committed throughput options if we consider Dedicated. Security will confirm log retention and any additional evidence (SOC2, penetration test reports).

If you can get a doc with contract-ready SLA and RCA timelines that would speed review. Tentatively the 2/18 slot looks OK; will confirm after procurement checks with our calendar.

—Alex

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: VentureTech competitive incident-response evaluation & next steps

Alex — thanks for looping procurement and security. I pulled together a concise comparison and some contract-ready language below. See the attached FAQ for more detail; I’ve pasted the key items inline to speed your review.

Redwood incident response & RCA (summary)
- Acknowledgement SLA (Sev1): within 1 hour (24/7) for Dedicated customers; Hosted API customers receive prioritization based on tier — enterprise plans include 24/7 on-call.
- Time-to-recovery (RTO): Depends on root cause; typical recovery for infra issues < 30 minutes with autoscaling/failover; application-level incidents vary.
- RCA cadence: preliminary findings within 72 hours, full RCA within 7 business days. Contract language we propose: "Redwood will provide initial incident acknowledgement within one (1) hour of detection for Severity 1 incidents and will provide a preliminary incident report within seventy-two (72) hours and a comprehensive root cause analysis within seven (7) business days, subject to reasonable extensions for complex investigations."
- Escalation & on-call: For Dedicated customers we provide a named PagerDuty escalation contact + a 24/7 on-call rota; for Hosted customers escalation is via our enterprise response team with SLA-backed routing. We can provision a test PagerDuty contact for the 2/18 window.

Comparative notes vs hyperscalers/other inference APIs
- Hyperscalers: strong network/infrastructure SLAs but often opaque incident ownership for multi-tenant managed services; RCA windows can be longer and involve cross-team coordination.
- Other inference APIs: variable support models — some offer 24/7 response only on premium tiers; many lack a clear canary/failover testing pathway for customers.

Suggested test plan (high-level)
1) Pre-test validation (30 min): verify log ingestion, alerting, and authentication flows.
2) Simulated outage (30–60 min): take a non-prod endpoint offline, verify failover, observe latency and token throughput.
3) Post-test debrief (30 min): preliminary observations and next steps.

Attachments: redwood-incident-response-FAQ.pdf (detailed wording), incident_response_sla_matrix.pdf (spreadsheet)

Neha — any security evidence you want us to include (SOC2 scope, pen test summary)?

If that all looks good I’ll draft the exact contract wording and share a one-page addendum you can attach to an MSA.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
